patch.value: Stabilise the changelog gate release date by deriving it from the calendar version instead of the clock

value.note: inserted the date-from-version flag after release-version-from-package in the changelog, changelog:full and changelog:check scripts; bumped pm-changelog to ^2026.8.17
changelog gate passes with the derived date

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: [{"body":"Proof at version 2026.8.23 (a non-today calendar version): without the date-from-version flag the generator heading was 2026.8.23 - 2026-08-24 (today clock date, the midnight-flip bug); with the flag it was 2026.8.23 - 2026-08-23 (the version own date, the fix). package.json was restored to 2026.8.24 afterwards and the gate re-verified green."}]

data.body: Proof at version 2026.8.23 (a non-today calendar version): without the date-from-version flag the generator heading was 2026.8.23 - 2026-08-24 (today clock date, the midnight-flip bug); with the flag it was 2026.8.23 - 2026-08-23 (the version own date, the fix). package.json was restored to 2026.8.24 afterwards and the gate re-verified green.

patch.value: Changelog scripts now derive the no-tag release date from the calendar version (pm-changelog ^2026.8.17). Proof at version 2026.8.23: without flag heading 2026-08-24 (clock), with flag heading 2026-08-23 (version date). Gate green at real version 2026.8.24: changelog:check ok, npm test 74/74 pass, coverage thresholds met, pinned pm health --strict-exit exit 0.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Completed the site coverage. The first pass patched only the package.json scripts named changelog, which left four of seven invocations of the generator unflagged: three in the release workflow and one in the release notes script in package.json, whose name does not begin with changelog. That is not cosmetic. During a release the workflow generates the changelog and CI then checks it, so with the flag on only one side an untagged version whose calendar date is not today would have the heading derived from the clock on one side and from the version on the other, and the release would fail on that divergence instead of on the stale date it was meant to remove. Enumerated by grepping every tracked file for release-version-from-package rather than by reading the scripts that looked relevant: seven sites in this package, four in package.json and three in release.yml, and the recount now shows four of four and three of three. Gates after completion: changelog full then check reports up to date, pinned pm health --strict-exit exit 0.

value.note: exercises the release workflow path that npm run changelog:check does not: asserts every generator invocation in every tracked file carries the flag, and shows the same probe version yielding its own calendar date with the flag and today's date without it
executable proof for the release workflow invocations, which the package.json changelog check never reaches

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: CodeRabbit was right that the linked test only covered the package.json invocation and never reached the direct pm-changelog commands in the release workflow. Added an executable check that does both halves. The static half enumerates every tracked file containing a generator invocation and asserts each file's flagged count is not below its site count, which fails when any single site loses the flag; verified by removing the flag from one of two release.yml sites and watching it report one of two and exit non-zero. The behavioural half runs the generator twice on the same probe version 2026.1.2, deliberately chosen so its calendar date cannot coincide with today, and asserts the heading is 2026.1.2 - 2026-01-02 with the flag and 2026.1.2 - 2026-08-24 without it, so the test states the defect rather than merely asserting the fix.
